mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the rate rise, or the rate increase is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment (PAYEMS) above the prior quarter's average coincides with rising investor sentiment and higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% from previous quarter average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or no significant correlation between PAYEMS surge and returns.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 2%, it indicates robust supply-side momentum that boosts equity risk appetite and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return advantage in 60 days despite INDPRO being above the MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months reduces uncertainty, lowering risk premiums and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when CPIAUCSL remains below 3%.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% signal a labor market tightening that raises policy patience and supports positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases for two consecutive months below 4%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both retail sales proxy (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above their respective 6-month averages creates dual demand momentum, predicting positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return correlation when both proxies are above MA.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (PAYEMS) below the prior month's level accompanied by rising consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3%) suggests labor market cooling and increased uncertainty, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Labor market softening with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive despite the described labor/inflation signals.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of falling industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates a supply shock, which typically raises risk aversion and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when INDPRO is in contraction.
